ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a triangular paper piece with a $60^\circ$ angle is cut to remove this $60^\circ$ angle, resulting in a quadrilateral. What is the degree measurement of $\angle 1+\angle 2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: As shown in the figure, \\
since $\angle C=60^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle A+\angle B=180^\circ-\angle C=180^\circ-60^\circ=120^\circ$, \\
therefore $\angle 1+\angle 2=360^\circ-(\angle A+\angle B)=360^\circ-120^\circ=\boxed{240^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a triangular piece of paper, with the vertex angle labeled 60°. An oblique line cuts across the two sides of the triangle, cutting off the small triangle containing the 60° vertex angle, leaving the quadrilateral below. ∠1 and ∠2 are marked at the intersections of the cutting line and the two side edges, and are the two upper interior angles of the remaining quadrilateral; the other two angles of the quadrilateral are the two base angles of the original triangle. Reasoning: Let the two base angles of the original triangle be A and B. Because the vertex angle is 60°, A + B = 180° - 60° = 120°. The remaining figure is a quadrilateral, and the sum of the interior angles of a quadrilateral is 360°, therefore ∠1 + ∠2 = 360° - (A + B) = 360° - 120° = 240°.
